question: How much is the first pistol round worth, and does the side matter?
answer: The winner of the first pistol takes the map 59.5% of the time, 57.1% from the CT side and 61.9% from the T side.
findings: Pistol 1 won on CT: map win 57.1% (56.1%-58.2%, n=8,809).
Pistol 1 won on T: map win 61.9% (60.9%-63.0%, n=8,716).
A team that wins both pistols wins the map 69.3% of the time (n=8,912). When the pistols are split, the P1 winner wins 49.4%.
Above the Elo expectation, P1 on T is +11.3 points and on CT +6.0. Winning P1 against losing it, Elo-adjusted, is +17.2 points (+16.0 to +18.6).
method: Map win % for the pistol round winners (rounds 1 and 13), with Wilson CIs. Team strength is a logistic model on pre-map Elo, and the pistol effects are average marginal changes with map-clustered CIs.
data: bo3.gg round data, S/A/B-tier pro maps, 2023-10-16 to 2026-11-02, 17,525 maps
split_check: P1 winner map win: 59.3% early (n=8,762) and 59.7% late (n=8,763).

chart.title: Map win % after winning a pistol round
